overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review a complaint before the chair responded and by deliberating by email among a quorum; other allegations were declined, untimely, or not violations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair failed to announce at remote meetings that they were being recorded, without naming specific meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the complaint does not identify any specific meetings where the Chair failed to make such an announcement, only indicating that such meetings were prior to January 5.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair conducted Board business alone outside open meetings.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent that the complaint may be construed as alleging that the Chair effectively made decisions that should have been made by the Board as a whole, this allegation goes to the authority of individuals such as the Chair versus the Board to take action on particular matters, which is not a matter governed by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair cut off and muted public speakers during meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, as it is within the Chair's discretion to limit public participation, he would not violate the Open Meeting Law by doing so during a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair blocked agenda items from being placed on meeting notices.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law imposes no obligation on chairs of public bodies to place items on a meeting agenda, unless a chair anticipates discussing a particular topic.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to review an Open Meeting Law complaint within 14 days before the chair responded.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it did not first meet to review the complaint before the Chair responded.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged a quorum deliberated by email and social media; emails from Nov 27 to Dec 4 and posts Nov 4 to Nov 25 were untimely.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the allegations with respect to these specific emails and social media posts are untimely and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Emails sent December 21, 22 and 23, 2020 among a quorum of Board members allegedly deliberated on a broadband contract outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating among a quorum via email.

allegations.summary: Emails on February 19 and 25 allegedly involved deliberation among Board members outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, because these communications were not between a quorum of Board members, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board member posts in a closed Monterey community Google Group allegedly amounted to deliberation by a quorum outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the posts by individual Board members were directed to members of the public who were members of the Monterey-Community Google Group, rather than specifically to a quorum of the Board.

remedy: Publicly release the December 21, December 22, and December 23, 2020 emails within 30 days of receipt of the determination, to the extent not already done.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: we order the Board to publicly release the December 21, December 22, and December 23, 2020, emails within 30 days of receipt of this determination to the extent it has not already done so.
